Author et al. in the paper "City-on-Web: Real-Time Neural Rendering of Large-Scale Scenes on the Web" [S1].

The claim lists several technical details regarding the 'City-on-Web' paper [S1]. All specific facts mentioned in the claim are explicitly present in the provided source notes and passages: 1) The representation involves baking high-resolution 2D planes and a low-resolution 3D voxel grid per block to compute the attribute function f_k,l (supported by notes and passage [S1] 'baking high-resolution 2D planes and a low-resolution 3D voxel grid in each block to get the attribute function f k,l'). 2) Only non-empty voxels are stored in a block-sparse format (supported by notes and passage [S1] 'Only the non-empty 3D voxels are stored using a block-sparse format'). 3) Binary occupancy grids are generated to identify occupied voxels (supported by notes and passage [S1] 'After generating binary grids to identify occupied voxels'). 4) The occupancy grid is downsampled using max-pooling (supported by notes and passage [S1] 'We downsample the occupancy grid with max-pooling'). 5) Textures are compressed into PNG format (supported by notes and passage [S1] 'compress textures into the PNG format'). 6) Voxel resolution is 512^3 and Triplane resolution is 2048^2 (supported by notes and passage [S1] 'We set the 5123 resolution for the voxel and 20482 resolution for the triplane'). 7) The method uses volume rendering instead of mesh rasterization, resulting in lower frame rates (supported by notes and passage [S1] 'our frame rate during rendering is lower compared to other methods... attributed to their rendering pipeline based on mesh rasterization, which is in contrast to our method, which utilizes volume rendering'). 8) Training rays are rendered to collect samples (supported by notes and passage [S1] 'we render all training rays to collect ray samples initially'). 9) Preserved samples mark adjacent grid points as occupied (supported by notes and passage [S1] 'The preserved samples are used to mark the adjacent eight grid points as occupied'). Therefore, every fact in the claim,
